decisions.reason: As a related extension of the firm's wafer and process-integration capabilities, it is likely kept because any performance shortfall is not severe enough to outweigh its strategic fit in a growing semiconductor packaging market.
This product is very close to the core carrier-wafer business, serves a clear customer handling problem, and likely meets aspiration levels with relatively low additional organisational strain.

Although technologically more uncertain and newer than A and B, it remains within the firm's established materials and packaging-wafer trajectory, so management would likely allow more time before abandoning it.
The off-the-shelf wafer brand is close to the established offer and can use existing production know-how and channels, making it likely to be retained unless results clearly disappoint.

Because glass-based circuit boards are more distant from the firm's narrow core offer, they are more likely to fall below aspiration levels and be dropped so resources can return to established wafer products and nearer-term developments.
